comparator.name: Biology (Biologie)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted Biology OER 2026–27, articles 11–12 and current 2026–27 study guide; checked 2026-09-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted OER specifies ten 6-EC compulsory first-year units, five 6-EC compulsory second-year units, two separate 6-EC obligatory restricted choices in periods one and two, and three 6-EC suggested choices in periods three, five and six instantiated with the first-listed eligible units. Year three has 30 EC genuinely open academic minor space, 6 EC Science Skills and a 24-EC Biology bachelor thesis. Zero-credit study/career orientation, lab safety and language assessment do not enter the 180 EC. The general prospective page still lists older first-year titles such as Bouwstenen van het leven and Systeembiologie and omits current credited modules; the adopted 2026–27 OER and study guide determine this pathway. Optional minors are not formal bachelor routes.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Twelve courses differ from the integrated route: conservation, environmental observation, biogeochemistry, delta water and remediation, and sustainability research replace much of the molecular-laboratory and human physiology sequence.

alternatives.concept: Examines cells, biochemical processes, genetics, infection and disease alongside the biological basis of brain function, physiology and data analysis. alternativeSelection.assessment: The integrated living-systems route is the closest feasible UCR response; an ecology/evolution curriculum and a biomolecular/health curriculum arise from distinct target-specific interest clusters. All three concepts have relevant 24-course selections, pass formal feasibility and differ pairwise by at least six courses. Neuroscience and bioinformatics remain separately identified interests, but no fourth alternative is permitted.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study disease mechanisms in organs; UCR covers multiple organ systems rather than the heart and circulation alone.
Both study advanced brain physiology, but UCR emphasizes cognitive neuroscience rather than solely human neurophysiology.
Both examine the structures and workings of cells; UCR is a general molecular cell biology course.
Both address organism physiology; UCR specifically studies adult human systems rather than plants and animals.
Both teach molecular biochemistry and metabolic reactions.
Both provide laboratory practice in molecular and biochemical methods.
Both examine genetic mechanisms, though UCR links genetics to pathology rather than a full genomics course.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Microbiologie & microbiomen jaar 1 component; its 6 EC and compulsory, elective or open status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Microbiologie & microbiomen component; its 6 EC and compulsory, elective or open status remain explicit.
Both introduce biodiversity and ecological variation, though UCR does not duplicate the VU field sequence.
Both address organism diversity; UCR specifically focuses on conservation.
Both explain evolutionary processes and adaptation.
Both examine ecosystems and their interacting components.
Both examine biological communities, with UCR focusing on marine settings.
Both examine global environmental change; UCR concentrates on climate change.
Both involve field-linked investigation, with UCR concentrating on a sustainable delta rather than general ecological fieldwork.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Vrije keuzeruimte / minor component; its 30 EC and compulsory, elective or open status remain explicit.
Both teach data handling and visualisation; UCR is general data science rather than the VU big-data toolkit.
Both use prediction and data analysis; UCR teaches general machine learning rather than biological forecasting.
Both teach methods for scientific investigation, but UCR focuses on statistical human research rather than biology-specific methodology.

notes.text: VU Biology requires both ecological field and biochemical laboratory work, microbiology and a 24-EC bachelor thesis, while it permits five credited second-year choices and a 30-EC open minor. UCR combines life science, ecology and data courses more flexibly, without claiming its general research or neuroscience courses reproduce the VU specialist microbiology, field placement or independent thesis.
